ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \triangle ABC$ is inscribed in $ \odot O$, $ \angle BAC=60^\circ$, D is the midpoint of $ BC$, and $ \angle AOD=166^\circ$, $ AE$ and $ CF$ are the altitudes on sides $ BC$ and $ AB$, respectively. What is the measure of $ \angle BCF$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $OB, OC$,\\
since $OB=OC$ and $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$,\\
thus $\angle BOD=\frac{1}{2}\angle BOC=\angle BAC=60^\circ$\\
$\angle AOB=\angle AOD-\angle BOD=166^\circ-60^\circ=106^\circ$\\
since $OA=OB$\\
thus $\angle ABO=\frac{180^\circ-106^\circ}{2}=37^\circ$\\
$\angle OBC=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$\\
thus $\angle ABC=\angle ABO+\angle OBC=37^\circ+30^\circ=67^\circ$\\
since $CF \perp AB$\\
thus $\angle BCF=90^\circ-\angle ABC=90^\circ-67^\circ=\boxed{23^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, with the center labeled O, and the three vertices of triangle ABC are on the circle: A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, and C is on the right side. Line segment BC is the chord below, and D and E are both on BC, with D close to directly below O and E close to directly below A. AE drops perpendicularly from A to BC, and CF connects from C to point F on AB, indicating that CF is perpendicular to AB. It can also be seen from the figure that if OB is connected, then ray OB is located within the interior region of ∠AOD. Reasoning: Connect OB and OC according to the method. Because ∠BAC=60° is an inscribed angle, the central angle it subtends, ∠BOC=2×60°=120°. D is the midpoint of chord BC, so OD is perpendicular to and bisects chord BC; at the same time, in isosceles triangle OBC, OD bisects the vertex angle ∠BOC, therefore ∠BOD=60°. From the positional relationship in the figure, OB is located inside ∠AOD, so ∠AOB=∠AOD−∠BOD=166°−60°=106°. In isosceles triangle AOB, OA=OB, so the base angle ∠ABO=(180°−106°)/2=37°. In isosceles triangle BOC, OB=OC, and ∠BOC=120°, so ∠OBC=(180°−120°)/2=30°. Therefore ∠ABC=∠ABO+∠OBC=37°+30°=67°. Also because CF⊥AB, ∠BCF=90°−∠ABC=90°−67°=23°.
